reason: The Ikeda map and Kerr bistability are a canonical system studied by both fields, not the same physical cause; shared object fits.
The isomorphism needs zero detuning (detuned lasers give complex Lorenz equations). NH3-laser chaos was only Lorenz-like, since it is optically pumped.

fix.summary: Haken (1975) showed that the Maxwell–Bloch equations of a resonantly tuned, homogeneously broadened single-mode laser (field, polarization, inversion) are isomorphic to Lorenz's convection model. A bad-cavity laser pumped far above threshold therefore shows Lorenz chaos. Lorenz-like chaos was observed in optically pumped far-infrared NH3 lasers. Class-B lasers reach chaos only with modulation or delayed feedback.
fix.breaks: Lorenz chaos needs the bad-cavity condition σ>b+1 and pumping many times above threshold, which ordinary lasers never reach. Detuning turns the equations into the complex Lorenz system. For convection the three-mode equations are a severe truncation, while for the laser they are close to exact.

reason: Deformation does not destroy all tori: for smooth boundaries, Lazutkin tori near grazing incidence survive. Chaos occupies a sea at moderate angles.

fix.summary: Rays in a dielectric microdisk follow billiard orbits. Deforming the circle destroys invariant tori at moderate incidence angles (Lazutkin tori near grazing survive for smooth boundaries). Rays in the resulting chaotic sea diffuse in the Poincaré surface of section until they fall below the critical angle and refract out. This explains the directional emission and spoiled Q of asymmetric-resonant-cavity lasers (Nöckel–Stone).

reason: Integrability holds only for the ideal fibre equation and needs the breaks given, so this is not an identity. The NLS soliton is the shared object.
The LLE is a mean-field (high-finesse) approximation. Pattern-formation theory transferred to microcombs; graduate nonlinear-dynamics courses rarely teach it, so strength 2.

fix.breaks: The LLE is the mean-field limit of the cavity round-trip (Ikeda) map. It fails at low finesse or strong per-pass nonlinearity, and higher-order dispersion, Raman and thermal effects add terms. The 'Turing' rolls are a finite-wavenumber modulational instability, not an activator–inhibitor reaction–diffusion system.

reason: The record needs a breaks (amplitude–phase coupling), so it is not an identity. The shared phase-locking dynamics is a mechanism.
Same equations with different physics, and a breaks is needed, so this is an analogy. The electromechanical analogy is mostly undergraduate material, so strength 2.
The coupled-mode equations are the rotating-wave limit of the pendulum equations with distance standing in for time, so this is an analogy. Classical mechanics graduate courses don't teach couplers.
Both photonic and mechanical topology were imported from electronic band theory (Haldane–Raghu; Kane–Lubensky). Mechanics did not take it from photonics.

fix.summary: Lattices of coupled resonators or waveguides and lattices of coupled pendula, gyroscopes or springs are all classical normal-mode problems. Both fields borrowed band topology from electronic systems (Haldane–Raghu 2008 for photonics; Kane–Lubensky 2014 and Süsstrunk–Huber 2015 for mechanics), so winding and Chern numbers predict protected edge modes. The SSH chain appears in both.

reason: Split-ring resonators and plasmons are specialist metamaterial topics; a classical mechanics graduate course would not teach the link.
The record's own breaks lists real differences (scalar vs vector waves, TEM mode), so the shared impedance form is an analogy, not an identity.
A specialist applied topic, structural in neither field's graduate core.
A broad 'nonlinear optics uses acoustic waves' link; acoustics courses don't teach stimulated Brillouin scattering, so strength 2.
Phase matching has no counterpart in the swing, so a breaks is needed. This is the same parametric-pumping mechanism, not an identity.
The averaging fails at relativistic intensities (a breaks is needed), so this is the same mechanism, not an identity.
No technique moved across. Inertial rotation sensing is studied by both, and the gyroscope note covers ring-laser gyros.
The breaks shows the dynamics differ (frequency independent of L), so this is the same torque-driven precession mechanism, not an identity.
Canonical coordinates fix only the Liouville measure. The factors N! and h^{3N} come from quantum counting, not from analytical mechanics.

fix.summary: Gibbs ensembles are probability densities on the canonical phase space of analytical mechanics. The Boltzmann weight exponentiates the Hamiltonian H(q,p), and the canonically invariant Liouville measure d^{3N}q d^{3N}p is the counting measure; the normalization N! h^{3N} is supplied by quantum mechanics. Each quadratic term in H then carries k_BT/2.

reason: Shared Legendre and Lagrangian-submanifold mathematics with different physics: thermodynamics has no dynamics or flow. This is an analogy.

fix.breaks: Thermodynamic state space is a contact manifold with no Hamiltonian flow or time evolution. Maxwell relations constrain equilibrium states, whereas generating functions define maps between phase-space coordinates.

reason: A 'Y uses X' derivation link: Hamiltonian dynamics is the setting of one proof, and stochastic proofs exist too. Not strength 3.
Chapman–Enskog is an asymptotic expansion that fails at finite Knudsen number. That is a mechanism, not an identity.

fix.breaks: Valid only for Kn≪1. Rarefied flows, Knudsen layers and high-frequency sound need kinetic treatment, and the higher-order Burnett equations are ill-posed.

reason: In 2D, long-time tails make the Green–Kubo integral diverge, so the relation fails in a regime and cannot be an identity.

fix.breaks: In 2D, hydrodynamic long-time tails (∝1/t) make the stress-autocorrelation integral diverge, so the 2D Navier–Stokes viscosity is not well defined.

reason: The conductivity exponent applies to lattice models. Continuum porous media (Swiss-cheese) have non-universal permeability exponents (Halperin–Feng–Sen).

fix.breaks: The universal conductivity exponent holds for lattice models. Continuum random media (Swiss-cheese models) give larger, non-universal permeability exponents (Halperin–Feng–Sen 1985).

reason: Lorentz reciprocity follows from the symmetry of the Stokes operator, which is the Onsager symmetry of the viscosity tensor. It is a mechanism and fails with odd viscosity.

fix.summary: The Lorentz reciprocal theorem makes the resistance and mobility tensors of particles in Stokes flow symmetric. That symmetry rests on the Onsager symmetry of the viscous stress tensor. Through D_ij = k_BT M_ij the same tensors give the symmetric diffusion tensor of Brownian suspensions, and Helmholtz's minimum-dissipation theorem parallels Onsager's least-dissipation principle.
fix.breaks: Reciprocity fails with fluid inertia (Oseen corrections) and in chiral active fluids with odd viscosity, which break time reversal much as a magnetic field gives Onsager–Casimir antisymmetry.

reason: 'Entirely' overclaims: at times shorter than about a²/ν, hydrodynamic memory (Basset force, t^{-3/2} tails) modifies the Stokes-drag Langevin picture.

fix.summary: The low-Reynolds-number drag 6πηa on a sphere is the friction coefficient in the overdamped Langevin equation, and Einstein's relation turns it into the diffusion coefficient. For a micron-sized colloid in water, inertia relaxes in m/γ ~ 0.1 µs, so on longer times colloidal Brownian motion is overdamped Stokes dynamics.
fix.breaks: At times of order a²/ν, unsteady-Stokes hydrodynamic memory (Basset force, t^{-3/2} velocity tails) makes the noise coloured. This was observed by Franosch et al. (2011).

reason: The virial theorem belongs in the conservation-laws note (it is in that note's scope), not in central forces and orbits.
Deep feedforward networks have an analogous, not the same, boundary, obtained by the same mean-field method with layer depth in place of time.

fix.summary: Sompolinsky, Crisanti and Sommers solved random recurrent networks with dynamic mean-field theory, a technique taken from spin glasses. At gain g = 1 the quiescent state gives way to chaos with a positive Lyapunov exponent. The same mean-field method, with layer depth in place of time, gives an analogous order-to-chaos boundary that governs signal propagation and trainability of deep networks at initialization.

reason: Molecular chaos is justified in the Boltzmann–Grad limit (Lanford) without invoking chaos, so 'backed by' overclaims; 'motivated by' is accurate.

fix.summary: Microscopic chaos is often invoked to motivate Boltzmann's molecular-chaos assumption: hard-sphere and Lorentz gases (Sinai billiards) are ergodic and mixing. Lanford's derivation, however, needs only the Boltzmann–Grad limit. The Gaspard–Nicolis escape-rate formalism writes a diffusion coefficient in terms of the Lyapunov exponents and the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy of the open system's repeller.

reason: Evans–Cohen–Morriss gave a heuristic Lyapunov-weight argument. Only Gallavotti–Cohen assumed Anosov dynamics. The topic is specialist, so strength 2.

fix.summary: The first fluctuation theorem (Evans–Cohen–Morriss 1993) came from simulations of deterministic, time-reversible thermostatted dynamics, using a heuristic Lyapunov weighting of trajectories. Gallavotti and Cohen proved it by assuming Anosov-like chaos (the chaotic hypothesis). In both, the phase-space contraction rate is the entropy production, and the SRB measure replaces the Gibbs measure in the steady state.

reason: Quasilinear diffusion K²/2 holds only for K≫1. Just above K_c, cantori make diffusion far slower, scaling as (K−K_c)^3.

fix.summary: Once the last KAM barrier breaks (K ≈ 0.9716), momentum in the Chirikov standard map spreads without bound, so a deterministic Hamiltonian map behaves like a Fokker–Planck process. Just above K_c, leaky cantori make diffusion slow (D ∝ (K−K_c)^3). For K≫1 it approaches the quasilinear rate K²/2, with oscillatory corrections. Accelerator modes and stickiness near islands make transport anomalous.

reason: The classical theory uses the classical r-matrix (the semiclassical limit of R). The quantum inverse scattering method quantized classical inverse scattering: a method transfer, not an identity.

fix.summary: Classical inverse scattering, with its Lax pair, classical r-matrix and infinitely many conserved charges, was quantized by the Faddeev school into the quantum inverse scattering method. There, commuting transfer matrices built from an R-matrix that obeys Yang–Baxter give Bethe-ansatz solvability, and the classical r-matrix is the semiclassical limit of R. The Lieb–Liniger gas is the quantized NLS field, and its attractive bound states are quantum NLS solitons.

reason: Network synchronization is a research-level shared object, not taught structurally in graduate courses of both fields; strength 2.
Localization of light in 3D disordered media remains disputed. Established cases are 1D and 2D light and 3D ultrasound (Hu et al. 2008).

fix.summary: Anderson localization is a wave-interference effect, not a specifically quantum one. The normal modes of a mass–spring chain with random masses are exponentially localized, with a localization length that diverges only as ω → 0, where acoustic modes survive. The same physics localizes elastic waves (including 3D ultrasound) and light in 1D and 2D disordered media; 3D localization of light remains disputed.

reason: Standing-wave thermoacoustic engines run a Brayton-like cycle. Only traveling-wave engines run a Stirling-like cycle.

fix.summary: A sound wave in a channel with a temperature gradient drives each gas parcel through a thermodynamic cycle of compression, heat exchange with the wall and expansion. The cycle is Brayton-like in standing-wave devices and Stirling-like in traveling-wave devices. Heat can therefore amplify sound (Rijke and Sondhauss tubes, Rayleigh's criterion) or sound can pump heat. Thermoacoustic engines and refrigerators are working heat engines bounded by Carnot.

reason: The quantum HJ equation differs from the classical one by Q. Bohm used HJ characteristics to define trajectories, which is a method transfer, not an identity.
WKB is asymptotic and fails at turning points and caustics. The HJ and action-variable machinery does named work in semiclassics; not an identity.
Van Vleck–Gutzwiller is a stationary-phase approximation that fails at caustics and beyond the Ehrenfest time. The principal function does named work there: method transfer.
Spekkens proved the contextuality–negativity equivalence for generalized contextuality and quasi-probability representations, not unconditionally. The link is narrow.

fix.summary: Classical Liouville mechanics with an uncertainty-like limit on what can be known about phase-space points reproduces Gaussian quantum mechanics, including entanglement and teleportation (Bartlett, Rudolph and Spekkens). The nonclassical resource therefore lies outside Gaussian QM: generalized contextuality, which Spekkens showed is equivalent to the absence of non-negative quasi-probability representations.

Newton's cradle showed absence of thermalization; GGE descriptions came later (Rigol 2007). FPUT is only near-integrable (close to Toda).

fix.summary: Classical integrable systems carry an extensive set of conserved quantities generated by a Lax pair. That is why soliton collisions are elastic, and why near-integrable lattices such as FPUT, which is close to Toda, recur instead of equilibrating. Quantum integrable systems (Lieb–Liniger, the quantum NLS) likewise fail to thermalize, as the quantum Newton's cradle experiment showed, and relax to a generalized Gibbs ensemble (Rigol et al. 2007).

record.name: Étendue conservation is Liouville's theorem for rays
record.summary: Rays obey Hamilton's equations with optical Hamiltonian −√(n²−p²), with transverse position and direction cosines times n as conjugate variables. Liouville's theorem then conserves étendue n²dA dΩ, so no passive optical system can increase radiance; this bounds solar concentrators (C ≤ n²/sin²θ).
record.map: H=-\sqrt{n(\mathbf q,z)^2-\mathbf p^2},\ d\mathbf q\,d\mathbf p=n^2\cos\theta\,dA\,d\Omega\ \text{conserved}
